passage:
A village turned off some streetlights near a river path for one month to help fireflies return. Safety lights remained at important corners, but bright lights near the water were reduced.
Some residents worried the path would feel unsafe. Volunteers guided evening walks and explained firefly life cycles.
When fireflies appeared, people were amazed.
The village learned that darkness is not always a problem. In the right place, managed carefully, it can be habitat.
The firefly path taught residents to think differently about light. Human comfort matters, but so do the needs of small lives that disappear when nights become too bright.
